beats.text: My landlord charged me for changing the lock he'd told me to replace.
beats.direction: Quiet disbelief. Sound like you are telling a friend, not announcing a headline.

beats.text: My key snapped inside the lock. My landlord was away, so he told me to call a locksmith and send him the receipt. I confirmed it by text before getting the cylinder replaced.
beats.direction: Matter of fact, easy conversational pace. Make the written confirmation clear without overemphasizing it.

beats.text: Then he listed two deposit deductions. An unauthorized lock change, and no spare key. I sent him his own messages. He said he still hadn't received the spare.
beats.direction: Restrained frustration and a little disbelief, without shouting or acting outraged.

beats.text: The shopkeeper downstairs showed me the sealed envelope he'd asked me to leave. He hadn't collected it.
beats.direction: Slow slightly as the explanation becomes obvious. Dry, understated realization.

beats.text: I sent him a photo. The next morning both charges disappeared. He promised reimbursement on my next statement. Now I follow every phone call with a text, so there is a written record.
beats.direction: Relieved but still wary. Let the final sentence land naturally.
